venues.d: The group's quiet precision, dropped into the restored heart of the old city.
The surest hands in the city — service you never have to think about, on its own beach.
Qatar's first all-suite house, inside the crossed-sabre towers — theatre with Raffles butlers.
A soaring twin-tower newcomer that took a Forbes Five-Star in its first year.

venues.n: Sharq Village & Spa, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel
venues.d: A low-slung Qatari 'village' by the sea — the calm, traditional counterpoint to the towers.

venues.n: Four Seasons Resort and Residences at The Pearl-Qatar
venues.d: A marina-side resort address on the man-made island, with Four Seasons ease throughout.

venues.n: The Chedi Katara Hotel & Resort, Doha
venues.d: GHM's understated design ideal beside the cultural village and its private beach.
A grand marina resort with its own beach and yacht berths — classic Ritz-Carlton scale.
A palatial Gulf-front retreat with the signature St. Regis butler on every floor.
New-city grandeur on the Lusail waterfront — polished, spacious, of the moment.
A landmark government building reborn as a members'-club-and-hotel with real buzz.
Maximalist, design-forward drama for the member who wants the volume turned up.
A high-energy design house in the business district — for celebrations, not quiet nights.
A spa-led vertical retreat with a sky-high pool over the downtown skyline.
A palace-scaled island house at the gateway to The Pearl — unabashedly grand.
The second of the crossed-sabre towers — gold-leaf glamour on a grand scale.

venues.n: Banana Island Resort Doha by Anantara
venues.d: A ferry-only island escape with over-water villas — the closest thing to a beach holiday off Doha.

venues.n: The Plaza Doha, LXR Hotels & Resorts
venues.d: A jewel-box LXR house in the walkable downtown quarter, all quiet polish.
A long-established beach resort with the city's largest private stretch of sand.
A polished business-district tower with Waldorf Astoria service at a gentler price.
Ducasse's French-Mediterranean, on the museum's top floor, with Doha Bay filling the glass.
Piedmontese cooking of real refinement inside the crossed-sabre towers — Doha's newest star.
The Leela's grand pan-Indian house — the first Indian restaurant to win a Doha star.
Sri Lankan and South Indian home cooking — hoppers, kari and roti done with real soul.
Northeastern Thai cooking with genuine fire and fragrance — a Bib-listed favourite.
Modern Qatari cooking under the museum's desert-rose roof — heritage, elevated.
Generous, aromatic Moroccan cooking — tagines and pastilla with a proper hand.
Bright Mediterranean and Levantine sharing plates in the Rosewood's newest room.
Characterful, generous Mediterranean cooking — a Beirut name that earned its Bib in Doha.
Vibrant, pocket-friendly Khaleeji cooking — falafel, lamb kofta and proper Arabic coffee.

venues.a: Four Seasons Hotel Doha, West Bay
venues.d: The largest Nobu in the world, floating over the Gulf — the black cod that conquered the planet.
The izakaya benchmark that never empties — precise, buzzy, endlessly reliable.
The Cantonese standard-bearer — dim sum and lacquered duck in a low-lit lattice room.
Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's Japanese, staged with Mondrian theatre.
Peruvian colour and pisco energy — ceviche, anticuchos and a room that never quiets.

venues.n: La Mar Doha by Gastón Acurio
venues.a: InterContinental Doha Beach & Spa, West Bay
venues.d: Gastón Acurio's seaside Peruvian — bright cebiches and a long beachfront terrace.
Riviera cooking and a room that has never gone out of fashion — the Niçoise classic.
The New York Italian-American theatre — tableside Caesar, veal parm and red sauce, done grandly.
The Sethi family's colonial-club Indian — smoke, spice and swagger, carried from Mayfair.
Jiggs Kalra's progressive Indian — familiar flavours, reimagined with a light modern hand.
Indian-Chinese and pan-Asian comfort cooking with a devoted local following.
Beirut's grand Lebanese table — an endless, generous procession of mezze.
Jean-Georges Vongerichten's playful, produce-led cooking in a jewel-box island room.
1930s-Shanghai glamour and pan-Asian cooking with real intent.
Qatari home cooking preserved and served with pride — a rare taste of the real thing.
I.M. Pei's last great commission, rising from its own island — the finest museum of Islamic art anywhere, and the building that told the world Doha was serious.
Jean Nouvel's interlocking 'desert rose' discs, wrapped around the royal palace — the nation's story told inside one of the most photographed buildings on earth.
The old trading heart of Doha, faithfully restored to its mud-rendered walls and lantern-lit lanes — where the city still comes to eat, haggle and sit past midnight.
Qatar's largest cultural quarter — galleries, an opera house and a 5,000-seat marble amphitheatre by the sea, all in one walkable seafront village.
Four restored heritage houses at the centre of the rebuilt old town — including Bin Jelmood House, one of the few museums anywhere to confront the Indian Ocean slave trade.
A four-square-kilometre island of marinas and Riviera arcades — the first ground in Qatar a foreigner could ever own, and the city's most European evening stroll.
The seven-kilometre crescent promenade that frames the whole city — walk it at dusk, dhows on one side and the West Bay skyline on the other.

venues.n: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
venues.d: The world's deepest collection of modern and contemporary Arab art — nine thousand works, and the first museum of its kind in the region.
The Middle East's first sports museum and one of the largest Olympic collections on earth — every Games torch since 1936, beside Khalifa Stadium.
One of the few places on the planet where the sea runs straight into the dunes — a protected inland sea reached only by 4x4 across the sand. A day trip your advisor arranges end to end.
Qatar's built-from-nothing future city — a mile-long illuminated boulevard, the crossed-sabre Katara Towers and a waterfront that only switches on after dark.
The parkland strung between the two great museums — sculpture by the water (Serra's '7'), the MIA café, and the city's best skyline picnic at sunset.
The bar level of the largest Nobu in the world — a three-storey pavilion over the Gulf, cocktails and tapas with the West Bay skyline in the glass.
The quietly assured lounge in the group's Msheireb house — considered cocktails and artisanal bites, in the calmest, most central address in the city.

venues.n: The rooftop bar at Raffles Doha
venues.d: Live soul and jazz and 360-degree views from inside the crossed-sabre towers — the highest, most theatrical drink in the new city.

venues.n: The lounge bar at Rosewood Doha
venues.d: A polished sky-lounge in the twin-tower newcomer that took a Forbes Five-Star in its first year — a smart, contemporary place to begin the evening.
